subject: Engineering decisions
title: Android baseline recorded (C1)
question: What was measured for Android baseline recorded (C1)?
method: Transcribed from the cited historical record. Units and precision follow the source.
finding: Cost: n=3, one APK install, about 3 minutes of device time, no teardown, no second device. Tolerances follow the spread seen (cold start 40%, PSS 25%, RSS 20%, Java heap 35%, native heap 50%) so a re-run does not fail on noise; a regression larger than that still fails `wf bench compare --suite android`.

rows: - Decision: cold start is launch to the app's first `ReactNativeJS: Running "main"` log line, read with `logcat -v epoch -e ... -m 1`, not `am start -W` (it reports a timeout on the 1.5-CPU device, so its 11.8 s was the timeout). Evidence: three runs on the shared slim device under the lease gave 3.98, 4.97 and 5.65 s; the first probe saw the process start at 1.2 s, the marker at 5.5 s and the app's first debug logs at 14 s, so the marker is the earliest point where our JS runs.

- Cost: n=3, one APK install, about 3 minutes of device time, no teardown, no second device. Tolerances follow the spread seen (cold start 40%, PSS 25%, RSS 20%, Java heap 35%, native heap 50%) so a re-run does not fail on noise; a regression larger than that still fails `wf bench compare --suite android`.
